summary: The paper describes the use of atomic layer deposited (ALD) alumina (Al2O3) as a structural material for micro-resonators. The ALD process uses trimethyl aluminum (TMA) and water as precursors. The ALD Al2O3 is coated with a chromium (Cr) layer for electrostatic actuation. The resonators are fabricated using a combination of ALD and e-beam evaporation techniques. The study focuses on measuring the resonant frequencies and quality factors of the resonators using SEM and AFM techniques. The results show that the ALD Al2O3 micro-resonators have a high quality factor and can be used for various applications such as sensors and actuators.
